intent: A reusable structural-oak material whose longitudinal faces and transverse ends are slices of one authored growth volume. It extends the accepted Met-door palette and the measured end-grain anatomy without photographic projection, random noise, damage, or AI-generated imagery.

colour_continuity.rule: Reuse the exact twenty observed wood colours and their broad warm, cool, dark, pale, ochre, and muted-red hierarchy.

white_oak_measurements.paper: Seasonal Cambial Activity and Formation of Secondary Phloem and Xylem in White Oaks
rules: Vigorous annual rings can reach two millimetres or more.
Suppressed annual rings can be as short as one hundred twenty micrometres and contain only earlywood.
Earlywood vessel diameter is 154 plus or minus 28 micrometres.
Latewood vessel diameter is 15 plus or minus 3 micrometres.
Latewood vessels occur singly or in radial multiples of two to four with dendritic arrangement.

white_oak_identity.publisher: USDA Forest Products Laboratory, Center for Wood Anatomy Research
rules: Large earlywood pores begin the annual ring.
White-oak heartwood vessels commonly contain tyloses.

ray_structure.paper: Wood Anatomy of Modern and Fossil Fagales in Relation to Phylogenetic Hypotheses
ray_structure.rule: Quercus alba has rays of two distinct sizes: uniseriate rays and very wide multiseriate or aggregate rays.

coordinate_contract.rule: Side faces and end faces must evaluate the same pith path and ring-radius table. No end-grain atlas may invent rings that do not continue into the longitudinal faces.

representation.band_limit_rule: A feature smaller than 0.85 texel receives an area-preserving filtered response and is never enlarged beyond 1.35 texels merely to remain visible.

layers.purpose: Off-centre pith, pith drift, explicit annual-ring widths, and one continuous radial coordinate sampled by every face.
Persistent Met-door warm, cool, dark, pale, ochre, and muted-red fields.
Finite authored ring-boundary accents with burial, fade, and flatten events; no global stripe comb.
Local coordinate deflection around the two branch intersections already owned by beam geometry.
Earlywood pore rows, latewood density, and two ray sizes sharing the same ring radii as the side faces.
Sparse normal and colour striations derived from measured broad-axe events without cutting new cavities.
Large deliberately low-contrast areas between selected anatomical accents.
